propositions: Source code comments accumulate unresolvable commit SHAs, run IDs, and dated incident narratives that rot over time due to Gerrit rebase-on-submit, retention windows, and code churn.

A net-new block-level detector scans comments and docstrings for rot-prone patterns (SHA-like hex ≥7 chars, run/job/thread IDs ≥8 digits after keyword, date+incident-verb combos) and accepts only cites to ticket IDs or external-context escape hatches.

All detector hits at HEAD must be remediated by either citing a ticket/epic/story/bug ID in the ticket system, dropping rot-prone tokens while preserving durable prose, or replacing SHA narratives with git-log-S-findable behavioral descriptions.

The CI guard must block reintroduced rot-prone refs, pass the remediated tree with zero in-tree suppressions, and be wired as a named step in the build-and-test workflow following check_*.py convention.

Detector unit tests must cover false-positive gotchas (sentence patterns like 'bug surfaced' and ticket-dir paths must not trigger; 4x4 grouped IDs and word-triple aliases must accept; escape hatch must be honored).

Post-implementation discovery of false-accept bugs in the word-triple-alias pattern (matching file paths like sync-hardening-proposal.md) and race-condition violations require refinement to reject path/extension context while accepting sentence-final aliases.
